card.name: Right before a person's name
card.fires_on: Small words, commas, or kin terms (nephew, uncle) in historical prose just before a named person or official is introduced. The next word is expected to be a first name or surname.

modes.label: Kin term before name
modes.description: A relative word such as nephew or uncle comes right before the relative's name.
modes.example: quote from Thomas Jefferson to his<< nephew>> Peter Carr in 1787

modes.label: Comma before appositive name
modes.description: A comma after a title or description, followed by the person's name.
modes.example: the Governor of Lublin<<,>> Stanislaw Winczinski,

modes.label: Linking word before name or body
modes.description: A small word like a, the, of, or to just before a named person or authority.
modes.example: seized by order<< of>> Governor Moore, of Alabama

card.writes: It pushes down name-like word starts such as Ada, Matt and Eth, so the following name is not predicted by this pole.
card.plain: It fires in history-style text just before a named person or official appears.
